title: Career Roadmap · Video Editor
summary: A Video Editor transforms raw footage, audio, graphics, animation, and other visual assets into polished videos for entertainment, marketing, education, social media, corporate communication, and digital platforms.

blocks.text: A Video Editor transforms raw footage, audio, graphics, animation, and other visual assets into polished videos for entertainment, marketing, education, social media, corporate communication, and digital platforms.

The role combines visual storytelling, editing techniques, pacing, sound design, color correction, motion graphics, and an understanding of audience attention. Modern video editors may also use AI-assisted tools to speed up transcription, remove background noise, generate captions, organize footage, and create rough cuts.
Key responsibilities

items.text: Review footage and select the strongest shots.
Assemble clips into a coherent narrative or sequence.
Trim scenes, refine pacing, and create smooth transitions.
Synchronize dialogue, music, sound effects, and visuals.
Perform color correction and basic color grading.
Add titles, subtitles, lower thirds, and motion graphics.
Resize and reformat videos for different platforms.
Work with directors, producers, marketers, designers, and clients.
Manage project files, media assets, backups, and export settings.
Revise edits based on feedback while meeting deadlines.
Use AI-assisted editing tools responsibly without sacrificing creative quality.

blocks.text: This roadmap assumes a three-year B.Voc programme. Adapt the sequence to the institution's actual semester structure.
Year 1
Foundation
Develop editing fundamentals and visual storytelling

items.text: Learn shot types, camera angles, framing, composition, and visual continuity.
Understand frame rates, resolution, aspect ratios, codecs, and video formats.
Practise importing, organizing, trimming, and arranging footage on a timeline.
Learn cuts, J-cuts, L-cuts, basic transitions, and pacing.
Study dialogue editing, audio levels, background music, and sound effects.
Learn basic color correction, exposure, white balance, and contrast.
Explore Adobe Premiere Pro or DaVinci Resolve as the primary editing tool.
Study storytelling principles, scene structure, and audience engagement.

blocks.label: Practical milestone
blocks.text: Produce a short montage, a one-minute promotional video, and a simple interview edit.
Year 2
Production
Build professional editing and motion graphics skills

items.text: Learn advanced timeline editing, multicamera editing, and footage synchronization.
Practise color matching, secondary corrections, and consistent visual treatment.
Learn keyframes, masks, tracking, compositing basics, and motion graphics.
Explore Adobe After Effects or equivalent motion graphics software.
Practise audio cleanup, dialogue enhancement, sound design, and mixing.
Edit content for vertical, square, and widescreen formats.
Learn captioning, typography, title animation, and lower-third design.
Understand proxy workflows, media management, backups, and project archiving.
Practise receiving feedback and managing revision rounds.

blocks.label: Practical milestone
blocks.text: Produce a polished brand advertisement, a short documentary segment, and a motion-graphics video.
Year 3
Job readiness
Develop a professional showreel and industry workflow

items.text: Complete an internship with a production studio, agency, creator team, or media company.
Edit complete projects from brief and footage review through final delivery.
Develop expertise in one preferred area such as advertising, social video, documentary, or motion graphics.
Learn client briefing, feedback management, file naming, and version control.
Practise delivery specifications, export presets, captions, and quality checks.
Use AI tools for transcription, rough cuts, and repetitive tasks while reviewing outputs carefully.
Build a portfolio that showcases different editing styles and storytelling skills.
Learn basic project estimation, licensing, copyright, and usage rights.

blocks.label: Practical milestone
blocks.text: Complete a professional showreel and a portfolio of at least four or five strong projects.

blocks.text: Recommended capstone project

blocks.label: Project
blocks.text: Create a 60–90 second professional brand or event film.
Deliverables:

items.text: Interpret the brief and define the target audience.
Prepare a basic storyboard or edit plan.
Organize footage, music, graphics, and other assets.
Produce a rough cut with clear storytelling.
Refine pacing, continuity, and transitions.
Improve audio and apply consistent color correction.
Add titles, captions, and motion graphics where appropriate.
Export versions suited to the required platforms.
Present the final video and explain key creative decisions.

blocks.text: Use footage, music, fonts, and graphics that you own, have permission to use, or are appropriately licensed.

blocks.text: Choose tools based on the kind of work the student wants to pursue.

blocks.label: DaVinci Resolve
blocks.text: Video editing, color correction, color grading, and audio workflows; offers a free version with substantial capabilities.

blocks.label: Adobe Premiere Pro
blocks.text: Professional editing workflows used across many production and marketing teams.

blocks.label: Adobe After Effects
blocks.text: Motion graphics, title animation, compositing, and visual effects.

blocks.label: Adobe Audition or equivalent audio software
blocks.text: Dialogue cleanup and sound editing.

blocks.label: Blender
blocks.text: Free 3D creation and animation for projects that need 3D elements.

blocks.label: Canva
blocks.text: Simple promotional video graphics and social media assets.

blocks.label: Frame.io or similar review tools
blocks.text: Feedback, review comments, and collaborative approvals.

blocks.label: Media management training
blocks.text: Proxy workflows, backups, codecs, and project archiving.
Recommended learning sequence

items.text: Learn one main editor thoroughly.
Develop audio and color correction skills.
Learn motion graphics fundamentals.
Add advanced compositing or 3D only if required by the chosen specialization.
Build projects that demonstrate the skills, not just software familiarity.

blocks.text: Software interfaces, licensing, and subscription plans can change, so verify current details with the official providers.

AI can speed up repetitive tasks, but editors still need to make decisions about narrative, rhythm, emotion, continuity, and visual quality.
By the end of the B.Voc programme, a job-ready student should aim to have:

items.text: Proficiency in at least one professional video editing application.
A showreel containing four or five strong projects in different formats.
Practical experience with dialogue, music, sound effects, and audio balancing.
A working understanding of color correction and basic motion graphics.
Experience producing videos for both vertical and widescreen formats.
Familiarity with codecs, frame rates, resolution, and export settings.
At least one internship or supervised industry assignment.
An organized portfolio with clear explanations of the student's contribution.
Basic knowledge of copyright, music licensing, asset permissions, and client confidentiality.
The ability to meet deadlines, accept feedback, and deliver revisions reliably.

blocks.label: Recommended first career target
blocks.text: Junior Video Editor.

blocks.label: Best initial strategy
blocks.text: Master one editing application, develop storytelling and audio skills, and build a portfolio that demonstrates complete projects rather than isolated effects.

blocks.label: Most valuable differentiator
blocks.text: The ability to turn raw footage into a clear, engaging story with polished sound, consistent visuals, and platform-appropriate delivery.

blocks.label: Long-term opportunity
blocks.text: Progress into senior editing, motion graphics, color grading, post-production supervision, creative production, or an independent video editing studio.
